summary: Port Royal is a fast push-your-luck card game where players flip cards from a shared deck into the harbor, deciding when to stop before a duplicate ship type busts their turn, then recruit sellable people or ships for coins and points. It's a snappy filler with real tension in deciding how far to push your luck each turn.
praised: Very quick to teach and play
criticised: Can feel swingy/luck-driven for a 'strategy' game
Limited strategic depth over repeated plays
End-game can drag as scores climb

interaction.kind: racing to claim cards from a shared harbor row before opponents do
interaction.detail: Cards revealed into the harbor are available to any player on their turn, so a good person or expedition card can be grabbed out from under you, and ship cards impose costs that can hurt whoever is unlucky when they're drawn. Each player's own tableau of hired people and completed expeditions is otherwise built independently.
interaction.said: Reviewers frequently mention the push-your-luck tension of drawing for a shared harbor row — 'someone else can snap up the person or ship card you were saving for' — and light 'take that' via ships that make you pay or lose coins.

sources: coins from crew hired in the harbor row
victory points from expedition cards completed with matching crew sets
scoring.how_you_win: Push your luck flipping cards each turn to grab coins or hire crew, spending crew sets to complete expedition cards; the first player to reach 12 victory points (from expeditions, adjusted by coin count) triggers the end and wins.
